    Show / Hide Table of Contents

    Transition animation

    NavElement has independent Show and Hide transitions. Each transition can combine Move, Rotate, Scale, and Fade channels, driven by LitMotion on a real-time scheduler by default.

    Popups use the same transition system but configure their Backdrop and Content as separate layers.

    Start with a preset

    In the UI Builder Inspector:

    1. Select the NavElement and open Transitions.
    2. Choose the Show or Hide tab.
    3. Select a Preset category and Variant.
    4. Click Apply.
    5. Open the Move, Rotate, Scale, and Fade cards to tune the copied values.
    6. Use the Play icon to preview the selected tab and Reset to restore the element's On Start state.

    Apply bakes the chosen preset into the current channel values. After the preset block loses focus, its category returns to None while the copied channel configuration remains. This makes a preset a starting point rather than a locked style.

    In hand-authored raw UXML, preset-category and the one-based preset-variant can also remain as runtime settings. Any manually enabled channel overrides the corresponding channel built by that preset. An out-of-range Variant is ignored.

    Built-in preset library

    The package contains 21 categories and 351 variants. Every variant includes separate Show and Hide definitions.

    Category Variants Category Variants
    Back 8 Basic1 25
    Basic2 25 Bounce 15
    Default 1 Discrete 20
    Drift 10 Drop 15
    Fade 25 Flip 10
    Ghost 10 Gradual 12
    Jelly 10 Organic1 25
    Organic2 25 Rotate 25
    Shake 10 Slide1 25
    Slide2 25 Spin 10
    Zoom 20

    Choose None when you want to build the transition entirely from manual channels. Preset variant numbers start at 1.

    Animation channels

    Channel UI Toolkit style Main values
    Move translate From/To reference, direction or custom pixel position, offset
    Rotate rotate From/To Z-axis angle and offset
    Scale scale From/To Vector2 scale and offset
    Fade opacity From/To opacity and offset

    Move provides edge and anchor directions such as Left, Top, BottomRight, and MiddleCenter, plus Custom Position. Direction distances are calculated from the parent content rectangle and the transformed bounds of the element.

    Note

    UI Toolkit rotation is 2D. Only the Z axis is applied; Y-axis rotation from a source preset is not available.

    Reference values

    Each From and To side chooses a reference:

    Reference Meaning
    Start Value The channel's captured rest/start value
    Current Value The resolved style when the transition is prepared
    Custom Value An explicitly entered value

    Offset is added to the resolved reference. Keep the final resting layout in UXML or USS: transform styles applied by the animator are cleared after completion.

    Timing and playback

    Every enabled channel has its own settings:

    Setting Behavior
    Delay Wait before this channel begins; must be zero or greater
    Duration Length of one cycle; default 0.3 seconds
    Ease LitMotion Ease value, or a custom Animation Curve
    Play Mode Normal, Ping Pong, Spring, or Shake
    Loops Additional cycles: 0 plays once, 1 plays twice, -1 repeats forever

    All enabled channels run in parallel. The longest finite channel determines when Show or Hide finishes. Infinite loops are forced to Ping Pong and never report completion.

    Caution

    Do not use Loops = -1 on a transition whose lifecycle must finish. Infinite Show prevents ShowFinished and Auto Hide; infinite Hide prevents the View from closing and can leave a popup Completion task pending.

    The default scheduler is MotionScheduler.UpdateRealtime. Animations and graph Time Delay outputs therefore continue while Time.timeScale is 0.

    Interruption and reversal

    UIViewVisibility tracks NotVisible, Showing, Visible, and Hiding, plus continuous progress. When Hide is requested during Show, or Show during Hide, the opposite transition starts at mirrored progress instead of restarting from its beginning. This keeps rapid navigation responsive.

    While LitMotion is active, the animator temporarily suppresses the element's USS transition-duration and restores it afterward, preventing two animation systems from fighting over the same styles.

    Hide mode

    When Hidden Result
    Display Applies display: none; removes the View from layout
    Visibility Keeps display: flex and applies visibility: hidden; preserves layout

    Both modes ignore picking while hidden. Move, Rotate, and Scale automatically request UsageHints.DynamicTransform; Fade requests UsageHints.DynamicColor.

    Reusable asset preset

    For code-driven reuse, create Assets > Create > UITK Navigation > UI Animation Preset and assign it through UIViewVisibility:

    [SerializeField] private UIAnimationPreset dialogPreset;

void Configure(NavElement view)
{
    view.Visibility.Preset = dialogPreset;
}

    An inline Show or Hide animation configured on the element takes precedence for that direction. Asset presets are most useful when a View has no inline transition or when adding animated layers from code.
